speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in; please describe your headache in detail, including its location, severity, and whether you have noticed any specific visual disturbances like blurred vision, double vision, or blind spots. Have you experienced any nausea, vomiting, or neurological changes such as weakness or numbness during this three-week period?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the exact location of your headache—does it feel like a band around your head or is it more focused in one spot like your forehead or behind your eyes? Additionally, how would you characterize the vision loss, and can you identify any specific triggers or activities that worsen it?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Intracranial Tuberculoma (Tuberculous Meningitis)

I have noted your history of headache and worsening vision, but a prior diagnosis of Tuberculosis based solely on these symptoms requires urgent confirmation. I need to see imaging to locate any space-occupying lesions or signs of increased intracranial pressure. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain_with_contrast.
